cards.text: The LORD speaks to Ezekiel, His prophet, and calls him son of man. God has been picturing Samaria and Jerusalem as two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah (Ezekiel 23:4). Now He asks Ezekiel if he will pass judgment against them.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to declare to Oholah and Oholibah their abominations.

cards.text: So God lays out the charges, and friend, this is one of those moments I keep my mustache real still. They have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands.

cards.question: God says the two sisters committed adultery with their ___.
Blood is on the sisters' hands. What did they do with the children they bore to God?

cards.text: And God isn't done. He says they did this to Him too: on that very same day, they defiled His sanctuary and profaned His Sabbaths.

cards.question: On the very day the sisters slaughtered their children for their idols, they stayed far away from God's house.

cards.text: Then God speaks right to the sisters. They sent messengers for men who came from far away.

cards.question: When the men from far away arrive, how do the sisters greet them?

cards.text: Then the sisters sit on a couch of luxury, with a table spread out in front of it. And what's sitting on that table should NOT be there.

cards.question: On that table, the sisters set God's ___ and His ___.

cards.text: A carefree crowd fills the place, and drunkards from the desert and men from the rabble put bracelets on their wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads. Friend, when THAT'S the guest list, you don't need a timer to know the batch is about to burn.

cards.question: God speaks of one sister as "her who had grown old in adulteries." What does that tell you about her?

answers.text: She's been unfaithful a long time
She's too old to be judged now

cards.text: The men sleep with Oholah and Oholibah as with a prostitute. Then the scene turns, and righteous men step in to sentence them.

cards.question: Why do the righteous men sentence Oholah and Oholibah?

answers.text: They are adulteresses with blood on their hands
They broke their treaty with the Egyptians
They refused to pay tribute to Assyria

cards.text: The Lord GOD says to bring a mob against the sisters and hand them over to terror and plunder. The mob will stone them, cut them down with swords and kill their sons and daughters.

cards.question: Along with everything else, the mob will ___ the sisters' houses.
God says this judgment will put an end to indecency in the land and warn all the women not to imitate the sisters' behavior.
God's last word: the sisters will bear the consequences of their sins of idolatry. Then what will they know?

answers.text: That He is the Lord GOD

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "her who had grown old in adulteries.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question itself says 'Blood is on the sisters' hands.' That rules out the two wrong answers, because selling the children or sending them to Egypt involves no blood. Only the right answer fits the setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 6 says that on that very same day they defiled His sanctuary. Defiling the sanctuary means they went into it, so card 7's false statement (they stayed far away from God's house) is answered before the baker reaches it.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The two-blank question asks the baker to guess the exact items on the table: incense, oil, bread, lamps or robes. All five are believable holy items, so nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out the pick. The blank order is also arbitrary, since nothing tells the baker that incense comes before oil. This is the same kind of detail guess as the Psalm 23 'anoint David's head with' bad example.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke 'you don't need a timer to know the batch is about to burn' puts the idea of burning in front of the baker. That nudges them toward 'burn down' on card 17, which asks what the mob does to the sisters' houses.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'stand guard over' is three words for a single blank. It is also longer than the two-word right answer 'burn down' and the other wrong answer 'move into'.

rule.text: Fill in the blank: the question has a blank for 1 or 2 words.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 23:45 is future tense: 'righteous men will sentence them.' Card 14 retells it as present action: 'righteous men step in to sentence them.' Card 16 keeps the future tense ('The mob will stone them'), so the walkthrough handles this inconsistently.
findings.question: In prophetic passages, may Papa Dorin retell a predicted future judgment as present-tense narration, or must he keep the text's future tense?
